lead: Every conversation carries information that isn't in the words. This lesson teaches you to read five concrete signals (voice, verbs, the way they tell it, resistance, and the speech of someone who has already decided) and what to do with each one the moment it shows up. Reading the other person starts with reading yourself.
objetivo: read the voice, the verbs, the way they tell the story, the resistance, and the talk of someone who has already decided, and act when each signal shows up.

aprende.t: Why reacting on impulse costs the sale
The five signals and what to do with each one
Open resistance with a question, not with a defense
Stop selling when they have already bought

hero_alt: Consultant wearing headphones on a video call, eyes closed for a moment, focused on the client's voice.

secoes.sub: On their own, each one can mislead. Together, they almost never miss. Click each signal.

nos.detalhe: Tone dropped: slow down and ask exactly about that point. Tone rose: follow along and go deeper, that's where the desire is. Leaned forward: stop presenting and agree on the next step.

"I should" (outside obligation, almost zero) → "I need to" (real motivation) → "I'll try" (maybe, a ready-made way out) → "I will do it" (commitment). The subject can be the same; the chance of it happening changes.
Story mode (characters, the day it went wrong): they're engaged; answer with a similar case. Solution mode (steps, systems, deadlines): answer with operational clarity and draw out a story.
None of these is a no. They're all doors, and most people walk right past them by answering the easy part of the sentence. Resistance opens with a question, never with a defense.
"When this is up and running, can we measure it?" It sold itself. Answer in one or two sentences and move straight to the next step with two dates.

secoes.legenda: Excited voice with a weak verb: enthusiasm without commitment, urgency is missing. Restrained voice with a strong verb: a decision made quietly, agree on the date.
secoes.dica: Before the five signals comes you: I notice what I feel → I choose what to do with it → I notice what they feel → I lead the relationship.

secoes.sub: What to do about the signals that are easiest to miss.

texto: A client may treat you badly for reasons that have nothing to do with you. If you answer in kind, it ends right there.
If you answer "I see, tell me more about that," you sometimes uncover a big problem hidden behind the rudeness.
"You said you should solve this. What would make it a must?" "When you say try, what makes you unsure?"
Almost always, the answer reveals the hidden objection.
"What if it doesn't work in our reality?" is fear of failing in front of others → "what would need to happen in the first few weeks for you to feel at ease?".
"Great, but we're different" means not feeling understood → "different how, specifically?".

passos.sub: how a won sale gets lost
texto: Stacking three benefits nobody asked for. Raising an objection he hasn't brought up and planting it in his head.
Talking so much that he starts to wonder what it will be like to work with you every day.

secoes.sub: Right after the conversation: from your notes to a reading of the five signals.

blocos.conteudo:
You are my analyst of sales conversations. Below are MY NOTES from a
conversation I just had. Analyze them using five signals: (1) voice and pace, (2) commitment verbs —
should / need to / will try / will do, (3) story mode × solution mode,
(4) resistance patterns, (5) phrases from someone who has already decided.
NOTES:
<paste your notes here, with his phrases as literal as you can remember>
Deliver:
1. A signal-by-signal reading, quoting the phrase that supports each conclusion.
   If there is no evidence for a signal, write "no evidence" — do not make it up.
2. What stage of the decision this person is probably in, and why.
3. Which gate is stuck: urgency, feasibility, trust, comparison or budget.
4. ONE single recommended action for the next contact, with the phrase ready to use.

secoes.sub: The five-minute habit and the reading it makes possible.

exercicios.texto: Right after your next conversation, set aside five minutes to write down literal phrases, not impressions. "He said: we already tried this and burned money" is worth more than "he seemed resistant."
exercicios.pronto: you have at least 5 client phrases in quotes and no line of impression without a phrase to back it up.

exercicios.texto: Paste your notes into the reading prompt. Ignore any conclusion that comes without a quote.
exercicios.pronto: every conclusion in the reading quotes one of your phrases, and you have 1 action with a ready phrase for the next contact.

secoes.sub: 4 questions. The explanation appears after your attempt.

perguntas.p: The client says: "once this is up and running, can we measure the results?" What should you do?
opcoes: Take advantage of the interest and present the other benefits
Answer in two sentences and tie it to the next step with two dates
Anticipate the objections he hasn't raised yet
perguntas.explica: That is what someone who has already bought says. From there, the only thing that ruins the sale is to keep talking.

perguntas.p: Which verb shows the greatest commitment?
perguntas.explica: "Should" is an outside obligation and "I'll try" already comes with the exit built in. "I will do it" is commitment.

perguntas.p: "We already tried something like that." Which response opens up the resistance?
opcoes: "Tell me what happened: I want to make sure I don't repeat that."
"Technology has come a long way today."
perguntas.explica: It's an old wound. Countering with an argument shuts the person down; asking shows you listened.

perguntas.p: Upbeat voice, but the verb is "I should." What does that indicate?
opcoes: Enthusiasm without commitment: urgency is missing
perguntas.explica: The signals are read together. High energy with a weak verb calls for going back to the urgency gate, not closing.

itens.t: Reading the other person starts with you
itens.texto: Reacting on impulse is what costs the most sales.
Should, need to, I'll try, I'll do it.

itens.t: Resistance opens up with a question

itens.texto: All that's left is setting the date.
